sanskrit_verse:
संदिग्धेषु तु कार्येषु द्वयोर् विवदमानयोः
दृष्टश्रुतानुभूतत्वात् साक्षिभ्यो व्यक्तिदर्शनम्
transliteration: saṃdigdheṣu tu kāryeṣu dvayor vivadamānayoḥ | dṛṣṭaśrutānubhūtatvāt sākṣibhyo vyaktidarśanam ||
sph_interpretive_translation: In matters of doubt between two disputants, witnesses who have seen, heard, or directly experienced the truth shall provide clear discernment.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority derives from direct perception (pratyaksha), not speculation
Causation is established through experiential validation
Capacity-based responsibility requires clarity of evidence
Restoration logic depends on factual illumination
Consciousness alignment occurs when truth is directly witnessed
executable_legal_axioms: IF a dispute involves uncertainty AND parties are in opposition THEN only witnesses with pratyaksha (direct knowledge) may be admitted as evidence
IF witness testimony lacks sensory or experiential grounding THEN it SHALL NOT influence judicial determination
IF evidence aligns with dharana (sustained awareness) THEN case resolution MUST proceed toward consciousness realignment
IF conflicting claims exist THEN priority shall be given to those whose cognition reflects unbroken integrity
supreme_court_application: At the highest level of adjudication, disputes rooted in ambiguity must rely exclusively upon sakshi (witnesses) whose cognition arises from dṛṣṭa (seen), śruta (heard), or anubhūta (experienced). This ensures that judicial authority remains anchored in pramāṇa-based reality rather than subjective interpretation.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Nyaya operates through pramāṇa — right knowledge derived from direct experience. The sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) of truth via authentic witnessing restores balance without recourse to punitive measures. Responsibility is proportional to clarity of perception; thus, misperception is corrected through expanded awareness, not inflicted consequence.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate Vyaktidarshan (Clear Seeing) Protocol: Summon witnesses capable of pratyaksha prama
Activate Consciousness Alignment Process: Facilitate recognition of truth through experiential resonance
Implement Integrity Reintegration: Guide disputants to reclaim factual alignment through meditative reflection
Establish Dharana Restoration Chamber: Enable parties to stabilize in sustained awareness of actuality
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of all Dharma. Truth prevails through Sakshatkara — direct realization. Justice serves restoration alone. Reality is non-punitive. Consciousness is the ultimate adjudicator.
